candidates.tagline: The startup replacing SpaceX with a really, really big gun (Jules Verne called)
candidates.story: Longshot Space Technology unveiled at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 its plan to fire cargo into orbit using a ground-based pneumatic cannon that would need to be approximately 6 miles (10 km) long — reviving the same concept the US and Canadian militaries tried, and abandoned, in Project HARP in the 1960s.
candidates.why_funny: The 'revolutionary alternative to rockets' they're pitching was already tried, failed, and the only thing left of that attempt is a rusting gun barrel in Barbados that's now a tourist attraction.
candidates.alt: Aerial NASA photograph of the HARP project's two massive space gun barrels laid out horizontally on test grounds in Barbados, seen from above, showing the enormous scale of the 1960s cannon-to-space experiment

candidates.tagline: Galway spent €28k replacing their beloved 'G' with a lowercase 'g'. The city is now flying the old one from buildings.
candidates.story: Galway City Council paid €28,000 to replace its beloved 1984 capital 'G' logo with a maroon lowercase 'g' that critics say looks like generic corporate branding; 'Keep the G' protest flags appeared across the city, a petition launched, and councillors objected — then on October 12 the council announced it won't track the total rebrand rollout cost, assuring the public it will be 'cost-neutral.'
candidates.why_funny: The city's proudest design achievement is now a citywide flag-waving revolt, and the council's response to 'how much is this going to cost?' was officially 'we won't be checking.'
candidates.alt: 'Keep the G' protest flags bearing Galway City's old capital G logo displayed on poles around Galway city centre, with residents opposing the council's rebranding to a new generic lowercase design
